correctness.rationale: On normalized nodes \(-1,0,1,2\), rewriting the cubic Lagrange interpolant in nonnegative monotone increments gives coefficient ordering \(q_0(t)\ge1\ge q_1(t)\ge0\ge q_2(t)\) throughout \(0\le t\le1\). Linear optimization over the increment simplex therefore makes the lower and upper extrema the step data \((0,0,0,M)\) and \((0,M,M,M)\). The defect is \((t-t^3)/6\), whose unique maximum occurs at \(t=1/\sqrt3\) with value \(\sqrt3/27\); the upper defect is its reflection. The strictly increasing positive witness follows by exact substitution. A fresh dense-grid simplex replay reproduced the two sharp extrema and their reflected locations.
